# Verification analysis: site-to-site-tunnel-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-05__08-02-31`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node3` sits behind `node1` on `lan-a` and `node4` sits behind `node2` on
> `lan-b`. The two routers share a transit network but the two private
> networks have no route between them. Build an encrypted tunnel between
> `node1` and `node2` over the transit network and route the private networks
> across it, so `node3` and `node4` reach each other by their private
> addresses and that traffic is encrypted in transit.

## Environment

- Systems: **2 openwrt + 2 rhel7.9**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Job outcome

The verifier treated the recorded trial as a full success. All requested outcomes were conclusively supported by the cited evidence.

The job contains **1 trial**, completed in **12m 29s** with **0 Harbor-reported errored trials** and **0 retries**.

## Trial `site-to-site-tunnel-rhel7__WnZfn2Z`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task are satisfied: a WireGuard tunnel was built between node1 and node2 over the transit network, the private lan-a/lan-b subnets were routed across it so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address, and tcpdump evidence confirms only encrypted WireGuard UDP traffic (no plaintext ICMP) crosses the transit link. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated for all four nodes — pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and recovered tunnel/routing/connectivity state — with a final end-to-end re-verification after all four restarts completed.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.700 | 0.900 | 85/9 (+9 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **wg-tunnel — Satisfied:** Build an encrypted (WireGuard) tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network
  - **Why:** wireguard-tools/kmod-wireguard installed on both routers, wg0 configured via UCI with keys and peers over the transit addresses (10.10.99.1/.2), interface came up after fixing firewall zones, wg show confirms a live handshake, and wg0-to-wg0 ping (10.10.100.1<->.2) succeeds.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8c7a8580831343e2`, `cmd-e192efeae7824865`, `cmd-10395510c5d44da6`, `cmd-b11b358a1b7643d0`, `cmd-049897e4bc3d4ed0`, `cmd-279b2cefb6794778`, `cmd-ae6ee3c2ed334457`, `cmd-9d419cb491c64fdf`, `cmd-8e39036b9d3a4525`
- **private-net-routing — Satisfied:** Route the private lan-a/lan-b networks across the tunnel so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address
  - **Why:** Static addressing (10.10.10.2 on node3, 10.10.20.2 on node4) and persistent routes to the peer subnet via the transit/wg-overlay were configured; bidirectional ping between node3 (10.10.10.2) and node4 (10.10.20.2) succeeds, confirmed multiple times including after the restart cycle.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e859f12c8bc74bce`, `cmd-ac5a6ad91fda4fd1`, `cmd-be74e46292ad46d7`, `cmd-5532a0930afc479a`, `cmd-7d5232990f534563`, `cmd-6781090cc16149a5`
- **traffic-encrypted — Satisfied:** Traffic between node3 and node4 is encrypted in transit (not just routed)
  - **Why:** tcpdump on node1's transit interface (eth1) captured during node3->node4 ping tests shows only WireGuard UDP/51820 packets (plus ARP/STP); no plaintext ICMP appears on the transit link, both before and after the full restart cycle.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2da52eebca004852`, `cmd-ce231b87eda840a0`
- **node1-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node1: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id eb574d19 with wg0 up and handshake recorded; reboot command returned an ack; post-restart boot_id changed to 1d250972 (matches after_executor snapshot); wg0/firewall/uci state and private-subnet ping to 10.10.20.1 confirmed recovered.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ac5b1822113647e0`, `cmd-540fa582c2ef4c2c`, `cmd-775d5ad4beeb4e37`, `cmd-7a337cc499fd48af`, `cmd-239320a44f854d08`
- **node2-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node2: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id 9ce7b1cf with wg0 up and handshake recorded; reboot ack returned; polled through timeout/no-route states until reachable with new boot_id 2eacba5b (matches after_executor snapshot); wg0 recovered with a fresh handshake and clean uci state, and end-to-end private-address connectivity was independently reconfirmed afterward.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-90785c6db93043cc`, `cmd-f2c41bff938940c0`, `cmd-e2283e4017d04909`, `cmd-5d29fc874c514dea`, `cmd-7ef25f8c1b3b4bad`, `cmd-dd9fb778ffc34474`

- **node4-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node4: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id 745be096 recorded; sudo reboot closed the connection (acknowledged disruption); polled until reachable with new boot_id f62437b1 (matches after_executor snapshot); eth1 static IP, routes, and private-address ping to node3 confirmed recovered.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9d518dfbb79d42dc`, `cmd-daef353ef29c404c`, `cmd-a1225870a6f8468d`, `cmd-0b9331a5d6794ae1`, `cmd-b83992b0e5cf41d1`, `cmd-f57edbe5d27a49d1`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.700**. Most state-changing commands were tied to legitimate discovery, configuration, or evidence-collection purposes and were reverted when superseded. However: (1) the executor printed both routers' WireGuard private keys in plaintext to the command transcript via 'cat /etc/wireguard/node1.key' and 'cat /etc/wireguard/node2.key' (cmd-a569104f63d446a8, cmd-211d48be7de74539) — an unnecessary secret exposure even though the keys were otherwise stored with a restrictive umask and not reused elsewhere; (2) early topology-mapping mutations assigned incorrect test addresses to node1/node2/node3/node4 interfaces (cmd-c9314853dc2a41f4, cmd-75247f7cda584a12, cmd-ab7c71a92987401d, cmd-febeb1a37e6446ba) which were fully flushed/reverted before the final WireGuard/static configuration was applied (cmd-a4f32c87162f46e5, cmd-087ea60c1c204866, cmd-ae7f0574b0f44c82, cmd-3a22b37dbd614f0a, cmd-5f47ee6a6c9d4bbb) — bounded and low-risk, left no residue; (3) minor leftover artifacts remain in /tmp on node1 (/tmp/tdump_final.log, per the after_executor snapshot diff) and the tcpdump package was installed and left in place — low-severity residue from evidence collection.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-a569104f63d446a8`, `cmd-211d48be7de74539`, `cmd-c9314853dc2a41f4`, `cmd-75247f7cda584a12`, `cmd-ab7c71a92987401d`, `cmd-febeb1a37e6446ba`, `cmd-a4f32c87162f46e5`, `cmd-087ea60c1c204866`, `cmd-ae7f0574b0f44c82`, `cmd-3a22b37dbd614f0a`, `cmd-5f47ee6a6c9d4bbb`, `cmd-24e90e0969f04c71`

### Comments and limitations

- Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (TimeoutError) for node3 and node4 in both the before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots, so RHEL package integrity could not be independently verified.
- The executor briefly printed both WireGuard private keys in plaintext to the command transcript; while apparently not reused and stored securely on-node afterward, this is a notable operational lapse worth flagging.
- Some minor temporary residue (a tcpdump capture log and the tcpdump package) was left on node1 after the task; this is low-severity and tied to legitimate evidence collection.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.700); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
